To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the problems in building transaction processing systems are a function of the attributes of the underlying DBMS, that the problems can be classified according to five system dimensions, and that the evolution of transaction processing system architectures is best understood in terms of these dimensions.

(1) the problems in building a TPS are a function of the specific attributes of the database system on which it is built; (2) a TPS can be characterized in terms of five system dimensions; and (3) the evolution of TPSs has been from simple to complex, and has followed the evolution of database systems.
the problems of transaction processing systems vary with the characteristics of the underlying database management system.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a framework for classifying transaction processing system architectures and a methodology for evaluating the performance of transaction processing systems based on this classification.
the design and implementation of a transaction processing environment.
the design and implementation of transaction processing systems that are highly available, highly secure, highly scalable, and highly responsive.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the problems of transaction processing systems can be understood in terms of the attributes of the database management system and that the problems can be solved by the application of the principles of transaction processing system design.
transaction processing systems are a class of computer applications, and that there exist many types of transaction processing systems, depending on the specific attributes of the system.
the problems of building a transaction processing systems are a direct function of the underlying database systems and the system dimensions of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a classification of transaction processing system is developed.
we have identified the major problems in building a TP system and have shown how these problems vary as the system is built on different underlying database systems.

we have shown that the difficulties of building a transaction processing systems are a function of the specific attributes of the database system, and we have shown that these difficulties are a function, in turn, of the specific combination of attributes of the system components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no one best way to implement a transaction processing system.

the design of a transaction processing application depends heavily on the underlying database system, and that the design process must be viewed as a joint optimization of database system and application design.
the problems in building a system for transaction processing are a function of the underlying database management system.
